title: A house head that fails the release pin leaves no durable trace
body:
## Summary
witness_finished drops a fetched house head that does not verify against the release pin with only an in-memory backoff; a forged or wrong-key head is indistinguishable afterwards from a lost fetch.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/witness.rs:83 filters the fetched head through `verify(&release)`; a failure bumps `Witness.failures` and `retry_at` (witness.rs:84-85) and returns Ok. Nothing is written: no audit row, no deal evidence. A head signed by the wrong key or altered in transit is the strongest evidence the buyer wallet can collect that the HOUSE (or something between it and the wallet) misbehaved, and today it exists only until the next restart. The prefix branch (witness.rs:88) drops an unverified prefix the same way while keeping the head. Fixed looks like: a bookkeeping audit row (e.g. `house.head_refused`, deal-less, typed fields only: epoch, row_count, the head hash, which check failed) written by table-ledger, classified as bookkeeping in history/classify.rs, and rate-limited by the existing backoff so a hostile relay cannot grow the log faster than one row per backoff step.

## Flow
- relay serves a head signed by another key
- start_witness fetches it; witness_finished filters it out (witness.rs:83)
- failures += 1, retry_at moves; no row, no event
- after a restart nothing says a bad head was ever served

## Expected impact
The owner and an offline verifier can see that the house served an unverifiable record; today only a shorter or rewritten VERIFIED head is evidence. Could break: the append-only log grows on a hostile relay unless the row is tied to the backoff.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused head leaves evidence
Before: unverified / tampered head: 0 rows written (pinned by glass_tests a_head_the_release_pin_does_not_verify_is_never_kept_and_the_wallet_backs_off, commit 03eae34)
After: predicted 1 row per refused head per backoff step; not built (needs a table-ledger write path outside this context)
Method: simulation - the instrument exists (the new glass test), the write lives in table-ledger/src/witness.rs which this round does not own
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/witness.rs:83 `let Some(head) = fetch.head.filter(|h| h.verify(&release).is_ok()) else {`
crates/table-runtime/src/witness.rs:84-86 failures/retry_at only, `return Ok(())`
crates/table-runtime/src/witness.rs:88 `let prefix = fetch.prefix.filter(|p| p.verify(&release).is_ok());`
instrument: extend glass_tests a_head_the_release_pin_does_not_verify_is_never_kept_and_the_wallet_backs_off: after the stranger head, assert exactly one `house.head_refused` row with the head hash and no deal_id; after three refusals inside one backoff window, still one row per step

title: Watched subscriptions promise a check that never runs without PayPal
body:
## Summary
With no PayPal connection, or when the rescue rules' agent key cannot be selected, the watch pass returns silently and every watched subscription stays "not checked yet - within a few minutes" indefinitely.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/rescue.rs `tick_rescue_watch` returns Ok without a read when `self.secondary.is_none()` (no PayPal connection) or when `select_agent(mandate.payload.agent_key)` fails. `rescue_watch_views` derives the state only from the watch row (`tries`, `last_failed`), so such a row is `RescueWatchState::Waiting`, which apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words.ts RESCUE_WATCH_STATE.waiting renders as "not checked yet - Your wallet checks it with PayPal within a few minutes." RescueWatch.tsx reads no connection state. The sentence is false for as long as the wallet is not connected, and the owner has no signal that the rescue detection they set up is idle. Fixed: the view carries why reads are not running (not connected / rules' agent key unavailable / paused), from the same conditions tick_rescue_watch tests, and the waiting row says so.

## Flow
- owner signs rescue rules and adds a watch with no PayPal credentials saved
- scheduler tick: tick_rescue_watch sees secondary None and returns Ok
- Rescue page: "not checked yet - within a few minutes", hours later still
- same with a revoked or missing Assistant key

## Expected impact
An owner relying on rescue detection learns it is idle instead of trusting a stale promise. Could break: the RescueBook IPC shape (bindings) and the mock must change together.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every reachable watch state is said truthfully
Before: 3 conditions that stop reads (no connection, agent key unselectable, paused); 0 of them visible in RescueBook or RescueWatchView
After: predicted 3 of 3 visible; not built (table-client type + bindings + words.ts + owner/RescueWatch.tsx, a sibling context)
Method: simulation - the stall was traced in code (rescue.rs tick_rescue_watch early returns vs rescue_watch_views); the fix crosses table-client, bindings and a sibling-owned client file
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/rescue.rs tick_rescue_watch: `if self.paused || self.secondary.is_none() { return Ok(()); }` and `if self.select_agent(mandate.payload.agent_key).is_err() { return Ok(()); }`
crates/table-runtime/src/rescue.rs rescue_watch_views: `None => RescueWatchState::Waiting`
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words.ts:670 waiting: 'Your wallet checks it with PayPal within a few minutes.'
instrument: rescue_tests: a watch added with r.secondary = None, three scheduler ticks, then rescue_book() - assert the view names the reason (red today: Waiting with no reason)

title: Four hand lists of agent slots and two missing-key rules for one lookup
body:
## Summary
The three AgentSlot variants are listed by hand at four sites, and the "which slot holds this key" lookup aborts on the first unreadable slot in service.rs but skips it in proof.rs.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/proof.rs:31-35 (`sign_proof`) lists [Negotiator, Shopper, Assistant] and skips a slot whose key cannot be read (`filter_map(...ok())`); crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:355-361 (`select_agent`) lists the same three and returns `unavailable` at the FIRST unreadable slot, before reaching the slot that holds the key; crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:193 lists them again (mandate_list), and the startup provisioning in service.rs:~214 a fourth time. table-client/src/lib.rs:140 has no `AgentSlot::ALL`. A fourth slot would be missed wherever the list was not updated, and a keychain read failure on the negotiator slot today blocks every shopper/assistant money step while the proof export of the same deal still signs. Fixed: `AgentSlot::ALL` pinned by a serde-variants test (as LadderRung::ALL is), one `slot_holding(vault, agent_key)` helper with one missing-key rule, used by both.

## Flow
- keychain read for agent.negotiator fails, agent.shopper is fine
- select_signer on a shopper deal: select_agent errors at the negotiator slot
- export_proof on the same deal: sign_proof skips the negotiator and signs

## Expected impact
One rule for finding a slot key; a new slot cannot be half-wired. Could break: table-client is a shared crate, so dependents rebuild.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one enumeration and one lookup rule
Before: 4 hand lists of AgentSlot; 2 lookup implementations with different missing-key semantics
After: predicted 1 enumeration (ALL, test-pinned) and 1 helper
Method: probe - sites counted by grep; the behavioural difference read from the two loops; not built (table-client pub type is outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/proof.rs:31-35 filter_map(existing_signing_key(..).ok())
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:355-361 `.map_err(|_| unavailable("Agent key unavailable"))?` inside the slot loop
crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:193-196
crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:140 enum AgentSlot { Negotiator, Shopper, Assistant } (no ALL)
instrument: runtime test with a vault whose agent.negotiator read fails: select_signer on a shopper deal must succeed (red today); table-client test pinning AgentSlot::ALL to serde variants

title: The four-run cap is a bare literal in two places
body:
## Summary
The agent run cap `4` is written as a literal in engines.rs (start_agent) and again in policy.rs (arm_policy_run); the rearm guard only stays correct while the two agree.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:149 refuses a start when `self.runs.len() >= 4`; crates/table-runtime/src/policy.rs:125 (arm_policy_run) pre-checks `self.runs.len() >= 4` to avoid a doomed start. If the cap in start_agent changes alone, rearming either stops early (cap raised) or keeps calling a start that refuses (cap lowered; harmless but the armed map never records it, so it retries every tick). Fixed: one `MAX_RUNS` const used at both sites.

## Flow
- raise the cap in engines.rs to 6
- arm_policy_run still stops at 4 runs; deals 5-6 never rearm

## Expected impact
Removes a silent coupling. Could break: nothing (same value).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the run cap
Before: 2 literal sites of the cap
After: 1 const, 2 uses
Method: probe - grep `runs.len() >= 4`: 2 sites; not built because engines.rs belongs to runtime-actor-and-engines
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Proof export reports its own internal failures as INVALID input
body:
## Summary
export_proof maps a failure to build the authority manifest and a failure to compute the evidence commitment to `invalid()`, the code for malformed caller input.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/proof.rs:22 `table_client::authority::manifest().map_err(|_| invalid())` and proof.rs:39 `bundle.evidence_commitment().map_err(|_| invalid())`. Neither depends on the caller's arguments (the deal id was already resolved by the ledger export); both are internal faults. INVALID tells the window the request was malformed, so the owner is shown a "bad input" outcome for a wallet fault and nothing distinguishes it in the fault stream. Fixed: `unavailable("Proof file could not be built")` (or a fault code), matching sign_proof's missing-key branch.

## Flow
- manifest() or evidence_commitment() returns Err (serialisation fault)
- export_proof returns ErrorCode::Invalid
- client treats it as a caller mistake

## Expected impact
The owner sees a wallet-side failure as one. Could break: a client branch keyed on INVALID for this command (none found by grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - internal faults are not reported as caller error
Before: 2 internal-failure sites mapped to Invalid
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - neither failure can be provoked without a fault hook; the instrument is that hook
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/proof.rs:22 manifest().map_err(|_| invalid())
crates/table-runtime/src/proof.rs:39 evidence_commitment().map_err(|_| invalid())
instrument: a #[cfg(test)] fail flag on Runtime (as fail_forecast in forecast.rs) that makes the commitment fail; assert ErrorCode::Unavailable

title: A house-wake guard can lose its reset to idle on a full actor queue
body:
## Summary
HouseWake::drop resets the house state with `try_send`; if the actor queue is full the reset is dropped and the house state stays Waking.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/pairing_relay.rs:66-76: the guard that restores `HouseState::Idle` after a failed or cancelled wake uses `self.actor.sender.try_send(...)` and ignores the error. Drop cannot await, so try_send is the only option there, but a lost message leaves `house_state == Waking` until another house command runs. The window shows the house as waking with no wake in flight. Fixed: record the pending reset on the ActorHandle (an AtomicBool the actor checks each tick), or send the reset from the async path before returning and keep the guard only for cancellation.

## Flow
- actor queue saturated (burst of commands)
- house_wake: api.wake() fails, guard drops, try_send fails
- settings.house stays Waking

## Expected impact
The house card never sticks at "waking". Could break: nothing user-facing; ordering of HouseStatus events.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the house state always returns from Waking
Before: 1 reset path that can be dropped silently
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - needs a saturated channel to observe; the instrument builds it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: actor test with a bounded sender filled to capacity, a relay whose wake() fails, then settings().house after draining: expect Idle (red if the reset is lost)

title: envelope_simulate linear find of each deal in the exposure list
body:
## Summary
envelope_simulate finds each listed deal in `exposure` with a linear `iter().find`.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/simulate.rs envelope_simulate: `exposure.iter().find(|d| d.id == deal.id)` per deal, then `exposure_for_deal(&exposure, ...)`, which itself walks the exposure list per deal. Replacing the find with a map lookup leaves the per-deal exposure walk, so the order stays O(deals x exposure).

## Flow
- N deals, E exposure rows
- find: O(E) per deal; exposure_for_deal: O(E) per deal

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer comparisons in the limits what-if
Before: O(N*E): find O(E) + exposure_for_deal O(E) per deal
After: O(N*E): exposure_for_deal O(E) per deal remains
Method: probe - read both loops; the dominant term is unchanged
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/simulate.rs envelope_simulate `let Some(counted) = exposure.iter().find(|d| d.id == deal.id) else {` and `exposure_for_deal(&exposure, deal.id, amount.currency(), now)`
